input.note:
**Root cause: AWS EC2 On-Demand vCPU service quota exhausted — cluster autoscaler cannot provision new nodes.**

**Evidence observed:**
- All 8 `feature-backfill-0522-*` pods in `ml-batch` are `Pending` with no node assigned.
- Each pod requests **12 CPUs** on the `batch-c6i-4xl` node group (c6i.4xlarge = 16 vCPUs each).
- The cluster autoscaler correctly triggered a scale-up (`eks-batch-c6i-4xl: 2→10`), but **all scale-up attempts failed** with the same AWS error repeated across all pods:
  > `FailedScaleUp: Could not launch On-Demand Instances. VcpuLimitExceeded — You have requested more vCPU capacity than your current vCPU limit of 256 allows for the instance bucket that the specified instance type belongs to.`
- The scheduler message confirms no eligible nodes: `0/12 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient cpu, 10 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector` [cite: tasks/debug/debug-application/debug-pods#debugging-pods-0].
- Since no new nodes can be launched, and the existing 2 nodes in the group are already CPU-constrained, there is nowhere to schedule the pods [cite: concepts/configuration/manage-resources-containers#my-pods-are-pending-with-event-message-failedscheduling-0].

**Why it happened:**
The AWS account has a hard On-Demand vCPU limit of **256 vCPUs** for this instance family. Launching 8 additional `c6i.4xlarge` nodes (8 × 16 = 128 vCPUs) would push the account over that limit given existing usage. This is an AWS service quota constraint, not a Kubernetes or manifest issue — which is why nothing changed on your side [cite: concepts/configuration/manage-resources-containers#my-pods-are-pending-with-event-message-failedscheduling-1].

**Fix — action required by the cloud platform team:**
1. **Request an EC2 On-Demand vCPU quota increase** for the `c6i` instance family via the AWS Service Quotas console or at https://aws.amazon.com/contact-us/ec2-request (as indicated in the AWS error message itself). The increase needs to accommodate the peak demand of this node group (up to 16 nodes × 16 vCPUs = 256 vCPUs for this group alone, plus all other running instances).
2. Once the quota is increased, the cluster autoscaler will automatically retry and provision the needed nodes, unblocking the pending pods.

**Short-term workaround (optional, while waiting for quota increase):**
- Reduce the Job's `parallelism` to fit within the 2 existing nodes (each has 16 vCPUs; with 12 CPU requests per pod, only 2 pods can run simultaneously on 2 nodes). Set `parallelism: 2` to allow partial progress at the cost of longer runtime.
- Alternatively, ask the cloud platform team to free up On-Demand capacity by terminating unused instances in the same account/region.
